rationale: Single replacement of the ResNet stem boundary model.resnet.embedder (call d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0), explicitly replacing the installed stem bundle trial-e9279012c6-param-9ac5fd08 which owns that exact call site, and re-binding it at half chunk size (stem_chunk_rows default 4; TaskSearch may probe 4/8). The installed stage-0 bundle trial-fd9bdc62a2-param-b6738601 is untouched and composes unchanged: it consumes the same [32,64,56,56] FP32 tensor this boundary returns. How previous-feedback shapes this attempt: trial-fd9bdc62a2 was ACCEPTED (quality pass, max_abs_error 7.6e-06, exact top-1, objective 177,409,024 vs parent 203,099,136, paired AB/BA with zero noise; coverage routes stem_microbatch_rows8 and stage0_microbatch_rows8 both verified with 8/8 reference invocations), so there is no rejected implementation to repair. The one concrete failure recorded in the feedback is the stage0_chunk_rows=4 screening endpoint violating the throughput floor (6,854.59 img/s vs limit 7,158.88). This attempt responds to that failure rather than repeating it: the targeted region is the stem, an order of magnitude smaller than stage 0 (per target-resources the whole stem phase is 552.3 us of CUDA over 20 kernels at rows=8: conv 321.6 + bn 80.0 + relu 63.0 + maxpool 87.7, versus stage 0's two full BasicLayers), whose rows=4 route already executed cleanly and quality-passed in the earlier stem parameter search; and the parameter domain is restricted to [4, 8] with 8 as the proven-safe point, deliberately excluding rows=2 because the static memory floors of the unchanged phases (~145.3 MB stage-0 phase, ~151.4 MB stage-1 phase) mean rows=2 cannot beat the rows=4 plateau while multiplying exactly the launch-efficiency loss that invalidated the stage-0 rows=4 endpoint. Measured facts: the accepted peak 177,409,024 B decomposes exactly as live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + retained workspace 8,622,944 + 4 x 25,690,112, where 25,690,112 B is one 32x64x56x56 (equivalently 8x64x112x112) FP32 unit; the previous search measured stage0_chunk_rows 8 and 16 at the identical 177,409,024, so the binding moment is outside stage 0; the stem phase is the only phase where three such units coexist in the observed aten sequence (full assembly empty+copy_, chunk conv_out 8x64x112x112, chunk bn_out 8x64x112x112), with the fourth unit not explained by static shapes - per-operator allocation attribution is an explicit unknown, plausibly a row-scaled cudnn workspace for the 7x7 stride-2 conv, which is a hypothesis, not an observed fact. Halving the stem chunk turns conv_out and bn_out into 12,845,056 B each while the assembly stays 25,690,112, so the stem-phase moment should drop from 4 units to 2 units + 2 half-units. Hypothesis to be tested by the evaluator's clean paired measurement: peak_allocated_bytes falls from 177,409,024 to approximately 151,718,912 (-25,690,112, -14.5%) if the unexplained unit is fixed-size, lower (toward the ~151.4 MB stage-1 / ~145.3 MB stage-0 floors) if it scales with rows; no gain below ~145 MB is claimed. Throughput expectation: the accepted version measures 8,506-8,538 img/s against the 7,158.88 floor (16-19% headroom) and rows=4 only adds four extra small conv/bn/relu/pool launches, but the stage-0 rows=4 precedent shows the constraint can break, which is why the safe rows=8 variant stays declared. Numerics: the stem operators (valid 7x7 stride-2 conv, eval BatchNorm, out-of-place ReLU, max_pool2d with the parent's [3,3],[2,2],[1,1] scalars) are per-sample exact on contiguous batch slices; a CPU replica of this exact composition over real Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU modules and aten.max_pool2d is bit-identical to the full-batch parent at rows 2/3/4/5/8 including remainder batch 7, and the identical pattern was accepted twice at max_abs_error 7.6e-06. Composition and coverage: the replacement invokes the unchanged Conv2d (11c99c108749a5d6fc1a0e93), BatchNorm2d (6b96219304ac79385e4ef06c) and ReLU (c98061ff56600d8872eade43) module parents and the aten.max_pool2d operator (0c8cafb1fc30de539c787552) through context.references on contiguous row chunks - the current-plan call IDs under this boundary - so every inherited call keeps executing with counts 4->8 per invocation at rows=4; a legacy embedder/pooler reference layout is accepted as a fallback at build, and if neither layout resolves build returns {} (concise setup failure) instead of silently routing every call to the parent. The replaced bundle's required call d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0 remains satisfied by this replacement at the same site, and its stem behavior (identical chunked composition, rows=8) is preserved by this code, so no inherited behavior is lost; runtime guards route unexpected args/kwargs, non-contiguous, non-float32, non-3-channel, CPU, requires-grad or training-mode calls to the parent with stem_parent_signature_fallback, and any exception inside the chunked path re-executes the whole stem through the parent reference (idempotent under eval/inference_mode) with stem_parent_runtime_fallback:<type>.

setup_work.build_time_gpu_work: none: build(context) only resolves context.references/context.modules for the stem boundary and its four current-plan children (plus the legacy embedder/pooler IDs as layout fallback), reads stem_chunk_rows from context['parameters'] (default 4, malformed values fall back to the default, minimum 2) and returns one closure; no tensors are allocated, no parameters are transformed, no model state changes, no fixture-dependent precomputation, no CUDA-graph capture. If the parent reference or both reference layouts are absent, build returns {} - a concise setup failure that installs nothing rather than silently making every call use the parent.
setup_work.first_invocation_behavior: the chunked path allocates through the normal CUDA caching allocator during the framework's 2 warmup invocations, so the recurring blocks (two 12,845,056 B chunk conv/bn transients at rows=4, the chunk relu and 3,211,264 B pool outputs, the 25,690,112 B [32,64,56,56] assembly, per-chunk cudnn workspaces) are already cached when the 5 timed repeats run; reset_peak_memory_stats() observes allocator reuse, not cudaMalloc storms. Every invocation recomputes from the current input through the parent callables - nothing fixture-dependent is cached.
setup_work.memory_scope: no CUDA Graph capture and no allocation migration into retained graph pools: every stem allocation stays inside the measured peak_allocated_bytes counter. Expected framework.peak_allocated_bytes ~151,718,912 B at rows=4 (hypothesis; graceful floors are the unchanged stage-0 phase ~145.3 MB and stage-1 phase ~151.4 MB) vs the accepted 177,409,024; framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes stays at its preparation-set ~280.3-280.6 MB because model preparation already peaks above any run peak, and setup adds nothing to either counter. Reserved pools may shift with the new smaller chunk blocks (prior stem evidence moved peak_reserved 429,916,160 -> 459,276,288 between rows 8 and 4); reserved memory is outside the objective and no counter decrease is claimed as a general physical-memory saving.

quality_risks: Numerics: cudnn may select a different conv algorithm at batch-4 chunks, reordering the 147-term accumulations and producing ulp-level logits differences; quality requires full 1000-class logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 predicted classes - expected to hold comfortably (eval BatchNorm, ReLU and max_pool2d are value-exact under row chunking, and a CPU replica of this exact composition over real Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU modules plus aten.max_pool2d is bit-identical to the full-batch parent at rows 2/3/4/5/8 including remainder batch 7; the accepted stem and stage-0 bundles measured max_abs_error 7.6e-06 at rows=8), but only the evaluator's reference comparison against offline-reference semantics decides.

Throughput: this is the concrete prior failure mode - the stage0_chunk_rows=4 screening endpoint measured 6,854.59 img/s against the 7,158.88 limit and was invalidated. The stem is far smaller (552.3 us GPU over 20 kernels at rows=8 per target-resources, doubling to 40 launches at rows=4) and the accepted version holds 8,506-8,538 img/s with 16-19% headroom, but if batch-4 kernel-efficiency loss plus the extra launches still break the floor, the declared stem_chunk_rows=8 variant reproduces the currently installed route exactly (peak 177,409,024, 8,506-8,538 img/s) so the existing TaskSearch/TPE loop can select a constraint-satisfying point without changing workload semantics; rows=2 is deliberately not declared because the unchanged-phase floors (~145.3/151.4 MB) cap its gain at ~0.3 MB while repeating the stage-0 failure mode at 16 chunks.

Fallback semantics: any exception inside the chunked path re-executes the whole stem through the parent reference (idempotent under eval/inference_mode: the parents never mutate the input views, verified CPU-side) and self-reports stem_parent_runtime_fallback:<type>; guards route unexpected args/kwargs, non-contiguous, non-float32, non-3-channel, CPU, requires-grad or training-mode calls to the parent with stem_parent_signature_fallback; missing references at build time return {} as a concise setup failure - the three categories stay distinguishable in route reporting.

Coverage and composition: the only replaced boundary is the stem; the Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU module parents and the aten.max_pool2d operator keep executing through context.references 8x per invocation at rows=4 (4x at rows=8), so the selection-listed stem-subtree calls (modules, aten conv2d/batch_norm/relu/max_pool2d, slice/empty/copy_ assembly, record_function hooks) keep executing with invocation counts 4->8; no calls are eliminated and no counter is filled with unused work. The earlier stem bundle trial-e9279012c6-param-9ac5fd08 is explicitly replaced as a whole (same call site), with its behavior preserved by this implementation; the stage-0 bundle at 595c8331c60823c132ca3a4a and every later stage execute unchanged, and the framework recaptures the plan after installation.

Memory accounting: if the statically unexplained fourth 25,690,112 B term does not shrink with chunk rows, or cudnn retains a different workspace for batch-4 stem convolutions than the current 8,622,944 B, the peak lands between 151,718,912 and 177,409,024 B; workspace retention and the exact 4-vs-5 activation coexistence are observable only through the evaluator's counter, which is why the 151,718,912 estimate is stated as a hypothesis with the unchanged-phase floors (~145.3 MB stage-0, ~151.4 MB stage-1) bounding any better outcome.

params.name: stem_chunk_rows
params.description: Contiguous rows per stem micro-batch within the frozen batch-32 request (remainder chunks handled generically; batch, workload and semantics unchanged). 4 (default) halves the stem-phase conv_out/bn_out transients to 12,845,056 B each, targeting ~151,718,912 B; 8 is the currently installed, proven route (~177,409,024 B, 8,506-8,538 img/s) kept as the constraint-safe point after the stage0_chunk_rows=4 endpoint failed the throughput floor at 6,854.59 img/s. rows=2 is excluded: the unchanged stage-0 (~145.3 MB) and stage-1 (~151.4 MB) phase floors cap its gain at ~0.3 MB over rows=4 while doubling chunk count again.
